Your money week: what to watch 📅

Three things land in the next few weeks:

⛽ Wednesday 4 November: the fuel levy relief starts. R1.50 a litre off petrol and R3 off diesel, and new pump prices take effect the same day.
🏦 18 November: Stats SA publishes the next inflation figure. September was 4.5%.
📊 19 November: the Reserve Bank decides on interest rates. The repo rate is 7.25% and prime is 10.75%. Economists are split on whether it hikes again.

What this means for you: a R1 million bond at prime costs about R10,152 a month. Every 0.25% rate hike adds about R170.

R370 grant vs the cost of food 🛒

The Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant stays at R370 a month. The MTBPS extends it for another year, with no increase.

Meanwhile, Maverick Citizen's 14-item food basket cost R390.86 in October, up from R388.86 in September. That's R20.86 more than the grant, before transport, electricity or airtime.

For a family of seven, the Pietermaritzburg Economic Justice and Dignity Group (PMBEJD) puts its Household Food Basket at R5,512.53 for October.

Fuel levy relief starts today ⛽

From today until 1 December:
• Petrol: R1.50 a litre off the fuel levy
• Diesel: R3 a litre off the fuel levy

Then from 2 December to 5 January 2027 the relief shrinks to R1 off petrol and R1.50 off diesel.

What it's worth: on a 50 litre tank of petrol that is R75 off. On a 70 litre diesel bakkie tank it is R210 off.

The levy relief is only one part of the price. Oil and the rand still move the pump price, so the official new price may not drop by the full amount. Check the Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources announcement for today's price.

Did your petrol cost go up or down at the pump today? 👇

Stress-test your budget before 19 November 🧮

The Reserve Bank decides on rates on 19 November. Nobody knows the outcome, and economists are split. A quick check now beats a surprise later.

1⃣ List every debt linked to prime: bond, car finance, credit card, store card.
2⃣ Ask: "Could I afford this if rates rose by another 0.25%?" On a R1 million, 20-year bond at prime, that's about R170 more a month (R10,152 to R10,322).
3⃣ Find the R170 now. Is there a subscription, airtime bundle or takeaway habit that could cover it?
4⃣ Start with the debt that costs the most. Credit and store cards usually charge far more than a bond.

Even if rates hold, you'll have built a buffer.

What's the first thing you'd cut to find an extra R170? 👇

General information, not financial advice.

text:
Why US interest rates reach your petrol tank 🌍➡️🇿🇦

Reports say the US Federal Reserve (America's central bank) left its rate unchanged on 28 October, but two members voted for a hike and traders were betting on one in December.

Here's the chain:
1⃣ Higher US rates make the dollar more attractive to investors.
2⃣ Money leaves emerging markets like South Africa, and the rand weakens. It was around R16.68 to the dollar on 28 October.
3⃣ Oil is priced in dollars. A R16.68 rand makes a R100 oil barrel cost R1,668; at R17.20 it costs R1,720.
4⃣ That R52 difference per barrel ends up in petrol, diesel and food prices.

Analysts warn the rand could pass R17 if oil and US rate pressures continue. That is a view, not a certainty.

Do you keep an eye on the rand? 👇

Your electricity bill: the next increase is already on the table ⚡

Eskom's direct customers got an 8.76% increase from 1 April 2026. For 2027/28, Eskom has proposed 8.83% from 1 April 2027.

That 2027/28 figure is a proposal. NERSA, the electricity regulator, has not made its final decision, and municipalities set their own tariffs on top.

What it could mean (illustration only): a R1,500 monthly bill rising by 8.83% becomes about R1,632, or R132 more every month.

A few ways to keep an eye on it:
• Check the tariff on your municipal bill
• Switch off standby appliances
• Ask your municipality whether you are on a prepaid or inclining block tariff

Is your electricity your biggest monthly bill? 👇
